the spectral asymmetry quantifies the gap inversion and that a fractionalization of spin occurs at the heterojunction between ACs with opposite spin inversion.

the excitation gap in a one-dimensional Andreeve crystal can close and reopen, leading to a sequence of gaped and gapless phases, that a spin-polarized interface can be realized at heterojunctions between neighboring gaped phases, and that this interface supports a fractionalized spin.

(1) the excitation gap of a one-dimensional Andreeva crystal can close and reopen, (2) a heterojunction between two Andreeva crystals can support spin polarized bound states, (3) the interface spin of the heterojunction can be fractionalized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of superconductivity and ferromagnetism in low-dimensional systems and the resulting novel phenomena.
the interplay between the exchange field, the spin-orbit interaction, and the superconducting order parameter in the context of one-dimensional ACs.
the interplay of topology and magnetism in one-dimensional superconductors.

the AC is a novel platform to study the interplay between topology, spin polarization, and the gap structure in one-dimensional systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how the interplay between the exchange field and superconductivity can lead to a rich variety of phenomena in one-dimensional systems, which may be of interest for the experimental realization and manipulation of spin-polarized states.

a periodic arrangement of ferromagnetic and/or antiferromagnetic regions in a superconducting wire can be a platform for realizing spintronic devices with spin-polarized transport and fractionalized spin.
a periodic sequence of ferromagnetic regions in an AC can be mapped to a single ferromagnetic region of the same size, but with a reduced exchange field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a spin-polarized AC can be used for the realization of spintronic devices with tunable spin polarization and spin transport.
a spin-resolved analysis of the AC spectrum provides an intuitive understanding of the topological properties and allows for the design of spin-filter devices.
the gap inversion can be used to control the excitation gap of a superconductor and the spin polarization of the bound states.
